verdict.tagline: Ripping through new mechanics takes time, but the slaughter opens up.
for_you_if: you master the new shield and parry systems
not_for_you_if: you expect the classic glory kill system
you lack ray tracing hardware and an NVMe SSD
you want free-form movement over structured combat prompts

claims.claim: Traditional glory kills and certain movement mechanics from previous entries are absent or significantly altered.

citations.review_text: Everything I enjoyed about DOOM 2016 and doom eternal has been stripped out. Glory kills are gone, the parry system is boring and requires only 2 braincells to use, and the story feels like it's been lifted out of another series entirely. It feels cheap and uninteresting and like a complete step backwards from the previous 2 games which were phenomenal.

I’m not sure, maybe I just didn’t give it enough of a chance, but from the first 30 minutes it feels like they took everything that made DOOM DOOM and just tossed it away.

The movement? Gone.
The brutality? Gone.
The weight behind everything? Gone.
That gritty, grimy, dark atmosphere? Gone.

And speaking of weight, even the guns have lost their feel. The shotgun feels like you’re shooting overly effective birdshot, and the Shredder feels more like a BB gun than something being fired by the Doom Slayer. The weapons just don’t have that violent punch behind them anymore.

And don’t even get me started on the finishers, because they’re basically nonexistent. No more constantly ripping demons in half, tearing limbs off, smashing them into paste, or chopping everything to pieces with the chainsaw. That over the top brutality was such a massive part of what made DOOM 2016 and DOOM Eternal feel so damn satisfying, and here it feels completely toned down.

You’re supposed to be playing as a demigod capable of ripping through Hell itself, but instead Doom Slayer feels like some obese space marine trudging around with a gun.

Maybe it gets better later, but first impressions arent great  and it wont get anymore than that from me, and comparing this to DOOM 2016 and DOOM Eternal, it genuinely feels like this should’ve been the game that came before them, not the successor.

It doesn’t feel like the next evolution of DOOM.

It feels like Diet DOOM.

one of the worst dooms if my opinion it has vary poor optimization and can barley runs with 8 gb of video ram and there's no glory kills if anything its like a Serious Sam clone with more mechanics not for me but i see how people can like it

claims.claim: Combat relies heavily on structured mechanics, quick-time events, and color-coded prompts rather than free-form movement and weapon choice.

citations.review_text:
To its detriment, [i]DOOM: The Dark Ages[/i] replaces [i]DOOM Eternal’s[/i] movement-based combat and weapon versatility with a heavier, more formulaic, and repetitive experience.

Every gun in Eternal had a role: Heavy Cannon for long range and Precision Bolt for weak spots, Combat Shotgun for short range and Sticky Bomb for Cacodemons, etc. Early on in The Dark Ages, I felt forced to use plasma—plasma shield enemies being the only encounter that seemingly needed a gun. This imbalance in gun viability—despite the variety of available weapons—is seemingly compensated for by a plethora of melee options. Sadly, these options are tied down to fixed solutions for each encounter.

Encounters are formulaic in design; once a solution is introduced, that encounter will play out the same way every single time. Encounters play closer to a rhythm game, where you must always press the right key according to the right coloured VFX or enemy. A large demon—larger than most encounters in Eternal—will appear just for it to sit there like a turret that spawns slow-moving rocks. The biggest of enemies feel more like entry-level Guitar Hero maps than they do DOOM—green, purple, and red VFX requiring different inputs/reactions. What this boils down to is a series of mechanic checks that become automatic. The rhythm at which you fight enemies is constantly interrupted by different encounter mechanics as well, making Dark Ages’ tempo inconsistent. Heat shield enemies in particular come to mind, as their two-part mechanic requires both guns and shield throw, making shield throw feel like a gimmick specific to that enemy type. These mechanics always play out the same, and any variance in play feels punished due to the wide gap in effectiveness.

Eternal is a sandbox by comparison: you’re given multiple tools, and it’s up to you how you want to solve each scenario. While there are correct answers to Eternal’s scenarios—as in, there is always the best option—they aren’t immediately obvious on…

Look how they massacred my boy... Doom is basically an on-rails QTE game now, just the key hints are slightly subtler. You see a row of enemies marching with red shields? Press R. An enemy is flashing? Press E. Green projectile? Right click. Almost no aiming or positioning required. Reminds me of another cult classic's dumbed-down version. Do you guys not have chainsaws?

It's not a hard, not recommended, but from someone who thought eternal went in the completely wrong direction with its highly direct rock paper scissors gameplay that just feels like the devs are poking you in the shoulder the entire time going, remember, against that enemy, you use this weapon, and against that enemy you use this single powershot weapon, but not the other 3, they don't do anything, and against that enemy you use this explosive, but not the other 4, they don't do anything. And to confirm their insistence on "Making you play the way we want you to play" they confirm weapon juggling was also an accident by hard blocking it in this game, which I didn't enjoy anyway because it makes the weapons completely meaningless as you're just scrolling through them regardless of situation and enemy.

In this game, it's even worse, as it's literally, a quicktime event. That's what the game is. Now press the green button; Good job. Now press the purple button! Good job! Now press the.....rinse repeat.
There is 0 exploration, as everything is marked on the map, yet somehow is a "secret", which is kinda good because they're stupidly large with nothing to actually do or explore. You're just running from arena to arena, another bad bit of eternal that's even more pronounced here.

Quicktime ages, is a blurry mess where nothing stands out from anything else, and it runs like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.

claims.claim: The opening moments feature frequent tutorial prompts and pop-up messages that interrupt gameplay.

citations.review_text:
I did not think it was possible to ♥♥♥♥ up a so simple task. This game feel like the marketing team breathing on your neck at every moment.
MAKE IT EASY. MAKE IT SHINY. MAKE IT SIMPLE.

It so annoying, they have there hand down your ass so much, that sometime i was wondering if i was the one playing or them.
There so afraid of any frustration from the player that they added additional life so that if you die, not really you can continue, and putting additionnal screen selection, destoying the rythme.

About additional screen infos, oh boy, you will have them for EVRYTHING. new weapon, meh first doom had them, it was destroying the immersion for each weapon, but meh, whatever, i can understand.
But now, you have them for each boss, telling you exactly how to kill it and how it will attack you...no discovery, no fun, just ♥♥♥♥ you player. You start skipping them as fast as you can, trying to not read them, just to keep the feeling of challenging a new mob.

Speaking of new mob, they added "small boss", the game has added so much move, dashing through half the map, paring, dashing , finishing a mob with "E" 25 meter away without problem , that the enemies are so blind of the epyleptic teleporting man in front of them, that you will kill "small boss" without realising they were one.
Before when you started going full "head-on" with enemies (no doging, no parying, just full i sho and you shot me back), it was a sign you were getting tired, and you had to pull yourself up again because you would die.
Now you can full box a big-belly-with-arm-gun-demon full front and still have enough for the next one.

It's a little sad, There is so much good choice in this game, the guy would invented the skull-crusher-gun need a kiss whenever he want, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ genius.
But damn. Discover new weapon or new ability, better prepare to have training ground each time on "please do this 3 time. NO. NO! you can't continue if you don't do as we want."

or the classic:
"HEY did you hear ?! you wil…

When this was announced, I didn't feel much hype for the game. Eternal was such a high point, and the game play for Dark Ages didn't wow me. So I waited for an adequate sale to come out, and when the price dipped to something more agreeable that $120AUD, i got it.

Sorry to say, this aint it.

There isn't any life in this game. I'm not feeling the same excitment i felt when i played 2016 or Eternal. Tutorial boxes come at you just as fast as the bad guys do, overexplaining overcomplicated skills, of which there were too many. Bash shield, throw shield, parry ♥♥♥♥ - whatever happened to just dodging out of the way? Oh right, you're supposed to just force your way through in this game. Unfortunately, thats not how Doom works. A turrent section in 2026? Did they dig this game play out of the early 2000s? Am i supposed to escort someone later on as well?

Hugo Martin's obsession with jager-style mechs is in full display here too. I played the first mission where you piloted said mech, and again, was left wanting. It was fun for a little while, but you just spam the same attacks and dodge the incoming attacks, the only time in the game a dodge mechanic is introduced. And there's several more segments later on? No thanks.

The ghost of Mick Gordon haunts this game. I can feel the lack of his presence from the very beginning. Finishing Move Inc, the production company who replaced Gordon, comes nowhere near his bombastic, heart pounding, adrenaline surging compositions of 2016 and Eternal, and that has four men working on the music here.  Four men failing, where one man pierced the stratosphere. iD, Bethesda, what were you thinking.

As for graphical fidelity, it's up there. But I had to upgrade my BIOS to play this game. If I have to do that, it means your game is overbred. For a fast paced shooter, I shouldnt need ray tracing and DLSS forced on. I know iD has a history of pushing the boundries of graphical fidelity, but we're talkling diminishing returns here. It looked …

I think I just need to accept that Doom really isn't for me anymore. I've absolutely adored the franchise all the way up to 2016, but I've just not been able to love it since.
But preferences aside, my experience around this game was absolutely grating.
I loved Doom for being a no nonsense, get-to-the-action kind of game, and this felt like anything but.
I spent 30 minutes faffing with drivers, and set-up before even running the game. But I kept running into massive performance issues, going back and forth, trying different drivers and trying to troubleshoot why it ran so poorly. After about an Hour I finally ended up with it running at around 20fps, so I could actually play the game.
After about an hour faffing with drivers and graphics settings I had the game running on Low settings and it still ran and looked awful, even on my Modern PC that runs everything else. Then, when trying to play the game I just felt myself being barraged by Tutorials. In my 20 Minutes of play I spent about 15 of them reading. Those five minutes of actual gameplay just consisted of me clumsily juggling all these mechanics that had been dropped on me. It wasn't fun at all.

I can't understand how this game runs so poorly on settings that make it look worse than a game that came out almost a decade ago, and how there is so much faff and friction to just playing the game. I think it's easier for me to just accept that maybe Doom isn't for me anymore.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the soundtrack lacks Mick Gordon's involvement and sounds generic or bland compared to previous titles.

citations.review_text: i wish there was a meh option. this just didnt hit like the last 2 6 hours in and i cant motivate myself to play it but ive played more doom 2016 and eternal since. and yes we all know the music sucks without mick gordon

I knew when bethesda screwed over and lost Mick Gordon, this was not going to be the same.

And it isn't. For all the wrong reasons.

For starters, the soundtrack is hideously generic and soulless. Yes, it's "hard" but if you actually enjoy music, you can tell it just disappears and adds nothing to the gameplay or world. That was a HUGE part of what made the previous two games work.

The aesthetic is insanely bland. It's piss-filter era ps3 bad. Monsters don't really have unique standout designs, they all look like an AI version (I know they aren't, that's just the vibe) of the originals. 

No glory kills. To some that may be a pro, to me it isn't, but what they replaced it with is universally worse - just generic "SMACK" where it's obvious your character's fist, foot or weapon isn't in the same county as the monster. Like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ kung-fu movie where nobody comes close to hitting anybody.

In the same way, weapons have no impact. There's a spread-fire machine gun that grinds skulls for ammo. Cool? sure. But it feels.... cheap? the super shotgun sounds like god slamming his car door and it does a billion damage but somehow it just doesn't feel like the gun is HITTING the demon hard.

The weapons too have no identity. In eternal they really refined the weapon to each have a role in taking out certain enemies. They reduced your ammo so you were forced to constantly be switching it up. And they intergrated the other mechanics for ammo and armor so well to make sure you were using everything in your arsenal and it became a literal dance of death. In this? nah. I can keep bouncing between the super shotgun and whatever they called the second plasma rifle and bounce between them forever against any monsters.

The upgrades feel soulless. 

The parry system feels cheap and not impactful. Combined with the weak melee damage that feels random whether or not it's going to do damage or not, you can literally get into a ping-pong slap fight with so many demons it's stupid.

The …

A slightly better game than I was expecting, but one that falls considerably short for numerous reasons when compared to the 2016 reboot and Eternal. Also the mandatory ray tracing has a notable impact on performance with no substantial visual benefit in return. 

The first big problem with The Dark Ages is the sheer lack of combat fluidity particularly compared to Eternal. This game focuses more on blocking and defensive parries for counter-attacking. There is also a lack of elevation and most combat encounters are in flat spaces. Level design is also really lacking for the most part. 

Weapons are also really boring and most lack punch even with upgrades. You don't really need to quick-swap in this game either as everything feels more simplified and defensive-oriented. Even glory kills have largely been omitted and replaced with basic non-cinematic animations. This is another huge step backwards. 

Other presentational issues stem from the generic, forgettable and largely unnoticeable soundtrack. There is no Mick Gordon music in this game and what is in place feels like some Temu copycat audio that is extremely bland and fails to elevate what is already mediocre battles. The atmosphere is mostly flat.

In a bizarre twist, for some reason the developers have tried to make this game more narrative-heavy with a story and long(er) cut-scenes. Sadly this is another aspect of the game that falls extremely short in quality across the board and is a completely needless inclusion. 

Despite some major woes, there is still some fun to be had here if you are a fan of the series. Expectations must be kept pretty low though. This is definitely not worth the absolutely ridiculous £70 price point and I would not consider it unless there is a significant deep sale in the £12-15 ballpark.

Eeeeeeh, the most boring doom I've played. This one just bored me in the long run. Those green and red colours just feels off, feels like they are launching some kind of tutorial attack like to learn but stucks the entire time. The level design is also kinda meh and boring.

The music was also downgraded of course we all know why but seriously the music is shy af in some parts. 

Aaaaaand the worst is, the executions, rip them. Basically they've added some but scripted and doesn't feel nice. Game doesn't deserve full price so won't recommend it.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that traditional glory kills have been removed and replaced with simpler or less cinematic melee animations.

citations.review_text:
Really wanted to enjoy this game. Love Doom and Doom Eternal... played them till I raged quit with difficulty. So when The Dark Ages was announced I was excited to play Doom, but with a shield and more melee... and what did I get?

1. Boring, inserted lore - I am the Doom Slayer... let me kill deamons trying to invade earth. I dont need the bad storytelling as well.
2. Its a more melee focused game WITHOUT MELEE WEAPONS. Just a pathetic punch and kick.

You may be thinking, but Daellym, surely they kept the cool executions like in the others.

NOPE! Sucker. Of course not. Now you just kick them flying instead of ripping them in half.

Then you get a giant robot to use (at least once)... hows that combat? PRetty cool right?

NOPE! Got you again... punch punch punch ♥♥♥♥♥♥ execution...

To be fair, if you play this one first and then the other Dooms, then you may play more than me. 

Some may say, you only played a few hours. Yeah. That is true. But I had to force myself there after the first hour was so underwhelming and painful comapred to Doom Eternal that I stopped.

A big step back so far. It’s just missing that raw energy you expect from a modern Doom game — it feels toned down and neutered.

Remember the huge cheers at the 2016 glory kill reveal? They clearly had a meeting at some point and decided, “Yeah, let’s remove that.”

I loved the intro in 2016 where Doomguy just yeets the tablet while some guy tries to give him exposition. It was a perfect throwback to John Carmack’s old line about story in games. It was there, but it knew its place.

Now we’ve got all this lore, no real glory kills, weak weapons, a lame parry mechanic, and side characters I couldn’t care less about.

They felt the need to explain everything, which completely baffles me. I thought we were dealing with Hell — incomprehensible darkness, pure evil manifest, a cosmic force of mindless malevolence.

Instead, they humanize Hell with scheming demon princes who make deals and play politics like medieval warlords.

That’s the real problem. Doomguy as an unrelenting killing machine makes perfect sense when Hell is pure, irredeemable evil. But once you humanize Hell and give it politics and motives, you undermine the whole fantasy. 

The Slayer goes from being a righteous force of wrath to just blindly slaughtering enemies that now feel like just another political faction.

They changed what Hell means, and in doing so, they broke what made Doom work.

Maybe that’s why they removed the glory kills.

Weapons are also really boring and most lack punch even with upgrades. You don't really need to quick-swap in this game either as everything feels more simplified and defensive-oriented. Even glory kills have largely been omitted and replaced with basic non-cinematic animations. This is another huge step backwards. 

Other presentational issues stem from the generic, forgettable and largely unnoticeable soundtrack. There is no Mick Gordon music in this game and what is in place feels like some Temu copycat audio that is extremely bland and fails to elevate what is already mediocre battles. The atmosphere is mostly flat.

In a bizarre twist, for some reason the developers have tried to make this game more narrative-heavy with a story and long(er) cut-scenes. Sadly this is another aspect of the game that falls extremely short in quality across the board and is a completely needless inclusion. 

Despite some major woes, there is still some fun to be had here if you are a fan of the series. Expectations must be kept pretty low though. This is definitely not worth the absolutely ridiculous £70 price point and I would not consider it unless there is a significant deep sale in the £12-15 ballpark.

No glory kills.
Mancubus doesn't get stunned.

Shield can randomly disappear into the ether even though I didn't block anything with it.
Superheating with the super shotgun barely works, doesn't work on the Vagary, or if it does it's horribly inconsistent. The Railgun has a stupid projectile arc that makes 0 sense, like a toddler throwing an apple. Pulveriser and Plasma gun just feel unsatisfying and ineffective.

No Mick Gordon so all the tracks sound samey and bland.
Enemies shoot through each other, and through terrain, and there's 0 demonic in-fighting. (I wonder what Carmack and Romero think?)

Need I say it again? NO GLORY KILLS, WHO IN THEIR RIGHT MIND GOT RID OF THOSE?! Fire them, immediately. The chainshield provided so much possibility, and all I got was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ disappointment.

If you want a decent arcade-style shooter, this may be for you, but if you're looking for a step forward from DOOM: Eternal, this ain't it, it's like they took one step forward and 3 steps back. I'm going to force myself to finish it and get all the collectibles, but if I'm being honest it's nowhere near as enjoyable or satisfying as DOOM: Eternal

TLDR: Bethesda ruins everything they touch, the dragon part was kinda cool, but everything feels hollow,  like someone on the team with a large say *has no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ clue what DOOM is all about*.

As a long time DOOM fan who's been playing since I was 12, finding the 2016 release on a shelf of the local CEX, falling in love with it immediately and pre-ordering Eternal as soon as it was on stores, I honestly have a few problems with this new game. But I'll start with the positives since it isn't like there wasn't many upsides to what they've done here.

In terms of visual appeal, it's stunning. The concept artists seriously hit the mark here. The guns look and move in a way that makes you want to keep shooting. The maps, especially the forge and the cosmic realm, are just mesmerising to stop and look at. And it's always impressive when devs make a background so stunning to look at in a game where you're supposed to be focusing on anything but. And the slayer honestly wears one of the coolest suits of armour I've ever seen, but I've felt like that with every new release lol

The shield bashing, throwing and parrying is especially fun. They've pulled off adding skill checks to DOOM rather well in that regard. And I seriously love the fact that if you land too hard it obliterates any fodder around you, the sort of immersive tanky feel you get from it is something I think would even improve the previous games.
And I also think the melee weapons are especially fun to use, getting to bash a huge monster in with your fist or any kind of melee weapon over and over again is always a blast.

But now for my main sort of quarrels with what they've done here:

--The story--
I think the storytelling is complete and utter pants. They make no attempt to explain any of the plot or worldbuilding outside of the codex entries, and even then the codex entries are being used completely wrong here. And in any other sense that'd maybe be fine, for example when playing through DOOM 2016, due to the surroundings like the UAC spokesperson and conversations with VEGA or Hayden, it was pretty obvious what kind of world/situation you were in and why. But in this game we're in Argent D'Nur,…

I bought this on sale. So the first issue with the game is the baked in raytracing, the game doesn't look substantially better than Doom Eternal and it runs very poorly on my machine. I don't have a crap machine either. I have a 5950X, 64GB and a 32Gig AMD 9700 AI Pro.

Secondly the combat is kinda boring after Doom Eternal. The guns are very meh. I am not sure how they managed to get this wrong after getting so much right in Eternal.

Thirdly. You can't explore the map properly. Often you get kinda trapped or their is a cutscene and you've missed items. In previous games you could travel through almost the entire map to search for secrets. There are other times where I was near and end of an area with the "point of no return marker", didn't walk onto the marker and was teleported away from that part of the map.

Finally the story is kinda meh. In Doom 2016 they had a lot of lore and mystery about who you are playing. This is all gone and most of the art style is very fortnite.

Don't buy unless on sale.
KEEPS CRASHING EVERYTIME YOU TAB OUT.

The game is fun, just wish it didn't crash every 15 minutes.
Tried on Windows with Nvidia GPU, tried on Linux with AMD GPU, tired different computers, tried fixes I found online. There doesn't seem to be a single scenario where the game actually can run without issues.

Long running fan of the DOOM series, I would've loved to have been to be able to play this game as well, even forked over the hefty price it took to get this game.
As fun as the first few levels were, I wasn't allowed much further in as updates caused the game to have worsening VRAM issues over time, eventually bringing it to a point to where I can't even reach the start menu without running into a crash. The visual fidelity is not enough of a leap over the previous titles or over other open-world games to justify gating people out of the experience entirely.
Good game, but it's poorly optimized for AMD hardware. Consistently crashes during gameplay!

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game relies heavily on a new shield mechanic featuring blocking and parrying during combat.

citations.review_text: I think this is by far the best of the modern Doom games, the parrying adds so much to the combat. Additionally, the level design is great, the visuals are impressive and the soundtrack is once again god tier.

This game is so satisfying. It does a great job of making you feel powerful without being invincible. I did not end up enjoying Doom Eternal and how frenetic it felt, but I loved the shield and parry mechanics in this game. It's my favorite of the modern Doom titles.

It's also metal as hell. It's like an 80's album cover come to life. It rocks.

DOOM: The Dark Ages is a great game overall, especially when it comes to its shield gameplay. In the main game, the shield adds a lot of variety to combat and makes fights feel fast, dynamic, and fun. Blocking, parrying, and using the shield offensively gives combat a different feel from previous DOOM games and keeps encounters exciting.

The DLC, however, definitely ramps up the challenge. The difficulty can be pretty intense, and some encounters feel much more demanding than the base game. I enjoyed the challenge, but it can sometimes feel frustrating rather than rewarding.

One of my biggest complaints is that the DLC switches around the settings and controls. Having to relearn where everything is after getting used to the normal controls is annoying and can really mess with your muscle memory.

Some of the secrets are also tedious to unlock. They can be fun to discover, but a few require more effort than they feel worth.

Overall, DOOM: The Dark Ages has fantastic, varied, and highly dynamic combat, with the shield being one of its best additions. The DLC provides a serious challenge, but the control changes and some tedious secrets hold it back from being as enjoyable as the main game.

4/5
Very good, high action gameplay. Not quite perfect, but a solid entry in the franchise.

*Note: the DLC has been announced, but not released upon time of this review. This is base game only.

Doom: The Dark Ages takes place prior to the events of Doom 2016, during a war between the Night Sentinels and the Demons of hell. The Doom Slayer is deployed during this war to rip and tear his way through the Demons. That's basically it. There is a story, but let's be honest, it doesn't matter. You're here to rip demons apart in glorious combat.

Gameplay is split into 3 sections: on foot, on dragon, and Atlan.
On foot is the vast majority of the game. Basic FPS stuff, move, shoot, blast demons. All that good stuff. While not as fast as Doom: Eternal, the slayer is still extremely mobile, and now has a Shield Charge allowing you to close the distance.
The shield is also the biggest change here - you can use it to block most enemy attacks, and with proper timing, parry others. Parrying charges your melee attacks which you can then use to combo after stunning the enemy. It makes for a fun, if repetitive, gameplay loop where you parry and counter attack. 
You can also throw it at enemies to quickly kill them, or to stun the larger ones momentarily while you move in for a kill.
Like Eternal, you also get your resources from the enemies - most will drop health if killed, and certain weapons will cause them to drop armor or ammunition as well. This keeps the gameplay moving. I was never in a situation where I felt I needed to scrounge for health because I knew the next encounter would provide me with the resources I needed. 
There are a large number of weapons. 12 in total, plus 3 melee weapons, and 4 upgrade runes for the shield. You can swap between all of these at will in the middle of a fight to match the situation as needed. 
They can all be upgraded as well with resources found in the game.
On Hurt Me Plenty difficulty, I found that the fully upgraded super …

A slightly better game than I was expecting, but one that falls considerably short for numerous reasons when compared to the 2016 reboot and Eternal. Also the mandatory ray tracing has a notable impact on performance with no substantial visual benefit in return. 

The first big problem with The Dark Ages is the sheer lack of combat fluidity particularly compared to Eternal. This game focuses more on blocking and defensive parries for counter-attacking. There is also a lack of elevation and most combat encounters are in flat spaces. Level design is also really lacking for the most part. 

Weapons are also really boring and most lack punch even with upgrades. You don't really need to quick-swap in this game either as everything feels more simplified and defensive-oriented. Even glory kills have largely been omitted and replaced with basic non-cinematic animations. This is another huge step backwards. 

Other presentational issues stem from the generic, forgettable and largely unnoticeable soundtrack. There is no Mick Gordon music in this game and what is in place feels like some Temu copycat audio that is extremely bland and fails to elevate what is already mediocre battles. The atmosphere is mostly flat.

In a bizarre twist, for some reason the developers have tried to make this game more narrative-heavy with a story and long(er) cut-scenes. Sadly this is another aspect of the game that falls extremely short in quality across the board and is a completely needless inclusion. 

Despite some major woes, there is still some fun to be had here if you are a fan of the series. Expectations must be kept pretty low though. This is definitely not worth the absolutely ridiculous £70 price point and I would not consider it unless there is a significant deep sale in the £12-15 ballpark.

Release the Slayer!

Doom: The Dark Ages is a pedal to the metal high octane adrenaline fueled first person shooter with some of the best combat in any game I've ever played. Doom 2016 was a great first step. Eternal, for me at least, has always been a bit too experimental and hard to fully enjoy. Dark Ages though? Absolute peak!

Good:

Performance is absolutely stellar. On my rig, at 1440p, locked 60 FPS with nary a drop in frames even when maps have upwards of 20 or more enemies all vying for a piece of the Slayer. ID Tech is without a doubt one of the best engines in use today for FPS gameplay. 

Combat is nothing short of near perfect. While parrying may not be everyone's cup of tea, I never once got bored of it. The sound when you reflect a projectile off your shield, or the impact of your boots hitting the ground creating a shockwave that turns lesser demons into chunks - glorious. Weapons are also well thought out and all have their uses, from the overheating accelerator or the wrecking ball that is the chainshot, to the classic super shotty that tears through anything, it's simply sublime. 

Level design is fantastic. Whether it's the large open arena fights with leader demons and their minions, or side areas with minor encounters or puzzles involving the shield, it's all well thought out and never comes across as ID being lazy just to get their work done for the day. The in-game map is also extremely well designed, with easy to read layouts and clearly placed icons that are overlayed with a checkmark once you've found the item, making it easy to know where you've been, where you haven't yet, and what you may have missed. 

Upgrades are meaningful and worth experimenting with. [h2]Doom: The Dark Ages — Review[/h2]
Apparently the character limit is too low for my entire review. I will leave a full version in a pastebin [url=https://pastebin.com/PBbAy7rE]here[/url].
[h2]Mixed Initial Impression[/h2]
I initially played the entire game on its launch date through Game Pass. This review was originally going to be a "Negative" review due to the lack of a "Mixed" option on Steam, as I was not particularly impressed with the base game, a sentiment I still stand by. However, the DLC massively changed my perspective on the entire product, which is reflected in my final score.
[h3]The Best: Performance[/h3]
Doom: The Dark Ages is a great game. In an era of half-baked releases and a plethora of issues stemming from a greedy AAA industry that is sucking the soul out of the gaming hobby, this game is a true outlier. It did not have any major issues at launch; it was a finished product that worked as intended from beginning to end.
[h3]Bad: Price & Forced Ray Tracing[/h3]
Let's get to the main negative that kept me from buying the game initially: its price tag. [b]$70 is a lot for a video game.[/b]
Another highly questionable decision was [b]forced ray tracing[/b]. Previous DOOM games ran perfectly fine on GPUs from the pre-RTX era. This game would surely have done the same if not for mandatory ray tracing, which likely locked a handful of players out of experiencing it entirely.
[h3]The Worst: Mechs and Dragons[/h3]
I know that piloting mechs and riding dragons is supposed to be cool, and the plot tries to lean into that power fantasy of a buff guy flying a dragon and crushing massive demons in a giant mech. However, these sections are simply not fun. They do not add anything meaningful to the experience and feel like filler missions designed to pad out the game length.
If you found them engaging, I am happy for you, but I certainly did not:

citations.review_text:
While the gameplay is great, it's very obvious that id Software have forgotten what made DOOM 2016 such a smash hit. Because Doom doesn't need cinematic cutscenes, or a in-depth story with characters, or vehicle sections or turret sections. DOOM 2016 just had you shoot demons because that's all Doom needs to be.
Also idTech 8 sucks as an engine, nobody asked for forced RT lighting minus tech YouTubers. Please return to idTech 7 or 6 for a future entry because they are far more performant and still look great.
Also make a new Quake game for the love of God.

After completing the main story and the DLC back to back I can recommend this game for sure but with a few criticisms. 
The base game was great and a different take on what DOOM is,  the mech and dragon levels were a nice addition if not a tad too long in a couple of examples. Performance was ok as you'd expect, but forced ray tracing is a strange one in a game like this where you're not really focusing on how it looks as you're moving about all the time trying not to die. And the emphasis on parrying is ok once you get the hang of it. With plenty of secrets and collectables to find with  fun and familiar weapons to use. 

One thing I didn't  like was the obsession with putting the "end game" doors in every single level in the DLC, which in some levels felt like they matched the main route doors, if not outnumbering them to get all of the secrets in a level etc. Personally, I would have had these as regular secret/ alt routes for the player to go as it became frustrating after awhile. And then have some other form of the 'end game' content. And I get it, as it's something extra for the player to do after the game has finished etc but idk, the implementation is a miss in my book. 

Sound track wasn't as good to Mick Gordon's masterpiece in DOOM 2016 / what he managed to do for Eternal either imo. 

Overall, 8/10 for me but F Microslop and I hope the people who were let go from ID after making an amazing trilogy of games get back on their feet, and I hope that we get more DOOM in the future but we shall see.

citations.review_text:
Definitely the worst game out of the trilogy (from 2016). That is to say it is still a very fun and good game for sure, just not as polished as the other two. 

Pro tip for if you are starting to get the hang of parrying: Turn of the slo-mo after a succesful parry. About that: The parrying works well but feels kinda off in a Doom game. idk what it is but it just feels like they were forced to do something radically different in fear of it just being too much of the same like the past 2. It does fit well within the theme they were going for however, and boy is that theme good. This one definitely has the coolest looking maps and areas in the trilogy. 

Because of the parry system and the movement in general this game feels less fluent than the previous ones. On top of that you have the big robot and dragon sections, which i didn't mind and enjoyed but i can definitely see why it can feel like taking the action and pacing out of the game. 

Now the only big downside i saw is the music. You can tell that it's not done by Mick Gordon. Also it seems more like generic metal on the background sometimes than something catchy or blood-pumpingly rhythmic. I only enjoyed a couple songs or so. You probably have to crank the music up a bit too since it's mixed quite softly. 

Besides that it runs amazingly and again, don't get me wrong, is an amazing game. I guess the bar was just so high because of the previous ones. I do believe however that if this came out as the first one of the trilogy the Doom franchise wouldn't have had as big of a revival as it did. 

Would advice to get on a discount too since i don't think it's worth the full price. And if you want to experience one of the newer doom games just buy 2016 or eternal since they're better (and cheaper).

Gameplay is fun, I liked the new parry mechanic, gives it a unique twist. It's a different game from 2016 and Eternal and that's fine by me, gives me a reason to revisit all of them. You can tweak the parry window so it challenges you just the right way, then it's very satisfying. Pacing of the battles is great, maps are varied and well built with some exceptionally cool ones that went places we didn't go so far in this franchise. Many maps are semi-open for you to tackle the objectives in any order which I can imagine is super cool for speedrunners as it allows for more depth of expression in routing these levels compared to the more corridor-like levels in previous games. The weakest-but-still-okay-because-short aspects are the dragon and Atlan segments, they lack the combat depth / variety of toolkit that the main game has. Took me 22h to almost-complete (see below) on Nightmare. Nightmare was perfect for me, with some fights requiring a couple restarts (like the optional fight in Belly) without it ever getting frustrating.

The collecting aspect was disappointing to me. Because the game knows you always have the automap, many collectibles are in unintuitive locations which are not signaled along the main walking paths, which makes it rather punishing to try and find stuff without help. As a result, if you play the game as intended rather than inventing house rules for yourself, the walking segments between battles degenerate into staring at the map and doing what is essentially very shallow side quests. The collection works best when the solution is decidedly not just a marker on the map, like the wolves (which actually had me taking a good look around these beautifully designed locations rather than staring at the bloody map) and some of the collectables in the Eldritch Horror levels (which require some light puzzling which I found to break up the pace nicely). I feel like in the first couple of maps you'd almost have a chance to find most collectibles withou…

bought on sale with the DLC, it was a blast and ran alright; turning on DLSS helped tremendously; 

i wasnt a fan of the mech or dragon flying segments, but i thought it was a fun attempt to do something new
i found the parry mechanics fun and enjoy the new the style of gameplay, and felt the exploration and puzzle segments were stronger than general combat, which was still very satisfying

The DLC stole the show in terms of gameplay and OST, I was really blown away by it; i wasnt sure how i felt about the chain spear first, but had grown to love being able to switch between that and the shield by the end

Good game, just not the best gameplay for me. Well and truly worth at a discounted price.

The presentation is the best they've ever done, the environments, cinematics and Slayer all look great, though the story itself is just alright. The gameplay is good but doesn't fully hit for me because of the stand-and-parry monotony which feels too easy/simple, however all the shield mechanics (Throw, Bash, Rune) are great fun, as well as playing like an unstoppable tank, though I do feel the lack of mobility/verticality. The Serrat (dragon) levels are a cool way to break up the gameplay, being able to freely fly around the map and then land for combat encounters on foot but the actual dragon combat is pretty meh. Similarly, the Atlan (mech walker) levels are also cool but too simplistic (though cinematic) in combat to make for engaging gameplay so being fairly short levels is welcome. Not sure I like Secrets/Collectibles being so obvious and telegraphed to you on the map that it makes it feel like you're playing it wrong if you don't get them so I ended up 100% every level making them feel more drawn out. Especially felt this with the new, divisive, big open maps design of this game, worst of which for me was level 6. I did like the change up and tricksy secret areas of the Cosmic Realms levels though.

The previous big Update (2) they made to add the setting for reducing the parry slow-mo effect, which I did down to 0, really helped with making the gameplay feel faster and flow better even though I do miss the glory kill animations from Eternal which now you only really get when you specifically attack an enemy from above or kill a boss. They also improved the weapon swap speed and more freely blocking in that update. Much appreciated and commended for listening and addressing feedback.

Compared to Eternal, for me, TDA loses the frantic (in a good way) gameplay that Eternal had in leaps and bounds. Eternal required you to always be on the move, regularly switch weapons an…

I want to write something nostalgic about id in light of everything that's happened, but this isn't the place for it. Instead, I think it's better to say something like this:

Doom: The Dark Ages is complete. With Revelations, this is the most perfect the game could be. The gameplay is superb, the graphics are stunning, the music works well with the game even if--as many have said--it's not as cohesive as Mick's.

If this is the last Doom game on idTech, then it's the last real one. I love this game, I've loved the studio since the 90s. If things go south from here, at least we got one last beautifully violent hurrah.

As a result, if you play the game as intended rather than inventing house rules for yourself, the walking segments between battles degenerate into staring at the map and doing what is essentially very shallow side quests. The collection works best when the solution is decidedly not just a marker on the map, like the wolves (which actually had me taking a good look around these beautifully designed locations rather than staring at the bloody map) and some of the collectables in the Eldritch Horror levels (which require some light puzzling which I found to break up the pace nicely). I feel like in the first couple of maps you'd almost have a chance to find most collectibles withou…

If, like me, you hated Doom Eternal's brainrot gameplay, TDA solves that.
It's a game that feels good to play and doesn't force you to run on meth brain, imagine that.
It still carries the terrible secrets system from previous entries, but it's not THAT obnoxious.
DLC is basically Eternal x Dark Ages, so if you didn't like Eternal, then you probably won't like the DLC either.

Good game, just not the best gameplay for me. Well and truly worth at a discounted price.

The presentation is the best they've ever done, the environments, cinematics and Slayer all look great, though the story itself is just alright. The gameplay is good but doesn't fully hit for me because of the stand-and-parry monotony which feels too easy/simple, however all the shield mechanics (Throw, Bash, Rune) are great fun, as well as playing like an unstoppable tank, though I do feel the lack of mobility/verticality. The Serrat (dragon) levels are a cool way to break up the gameplay, being able to freely fly around the map and then land for combat encounters on foot but the actual dragon combat is pretty meh. Similarly, the Atlan (mech walker) levels are also cool but too simplistic (though cinematic) in combat to make for engaging gameplay so being fairly short levels is welcome. Not sure I like Secrets/Collectibles being so obvious and telegraphed to you on the map that it makes it feel like you're playing it wrong if you don't get them so I ended up 100% every level making them feel more drawn out. Especially felt this with the new, divisive, big open maps design of this game, worst of which for me was level 6. I did like the change up and tricksy secret areas of the Cosmic Realms levels though.

The previous big Update (2) they made to add the setting for reducing the parry slow-mo effect, which I did down to 0, really helped with making the gameplay feel faster and flow better even though I do miss the glory kill animations from Eternal which now you only really get when you specifically attack an enemy from above or kill a boss. They also improved the weapon swap speed and more freely blocking in that update. Much appreciated and commended for listening and addressing feedback.

Compared to Eternal, for me, TDA loses the frantic (in a good way) gameplay that Eternal had in leaps and bounds. Eternal required you to always be on the move, regularly switch weapons an…

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the combat heavily emphasizes a shield and parry mechanic.

citations.review_text: Excellent, the gameplay is near perfection. Game is stable and runs well. One small nitpick I can have about the base game is that there's a bit too much parrying. The DLC fixes that by giving you more flexibility so you can parry or dodge.

Gameplay is fun, I liked the new parry mechanic, gives it a unique twist. It's a different game from 2016 and Eternal and that's fine by me, gives me a reason to revisit all of them. You can tweak the parry window so it challenges you just the right way, then it's very satisfying. Pacing of the battles is great, maps are varied and well built with some exceptionally cool ones that went places we didn't go so far in this franchise. Many maps are semi-open for you to tackle the objectives in any order which I can imagine is super cool for speedrunners as it allows for more depth of expression in routing these levels compared to the more corridor-like levels in previous games. The weakest-but-still-okay-because-short aspects are the dragon and Atlan segments, they lack the combat depth / variety of toolkit that the main game has. Took me 22h to almost-complete (see below) on Nightmare. Nightmare was perfect for me, with some fights requiring a couple restarts (like the optional fight in Belly) without it ever getting frustrating.

Because the game knows you always have the automap, many collectibles are in unintuitive locations which are not signaled along the main walking paths, which makes it rather punishing to try and find stuff without help. The collection works best when the solution is decidedly not just a marker on the map, like the wolves (which actually had me taking a good look around these beautifully designed locations rather than staring at the bloody map) and some of the collectables in the Eldritch Horror levels (which require some light puzzling which I found to break up the pace nicely). I feel like in the first couple of maps you'd almost have a chance to find most collectibles withou…

Despite all the controversy, it's a solid and enjoyable Doom game.

GOOD

1. It's as fast as Eternal if you play it via run-n-gun method and push through enemies like a jet engine tank
2. Every single gun is viable as a primary
3. Very satisfying feeling of smashing entire demon armies in a few minutes head on
4. A certain Cosmic Dimension being very creative with level design and puzzles
5. Exploration is good 

BAD

1. Overreliance on Shield - Dark Ages substitutes every mechanic with something out of the three available actions - Shield Throw/Shield Bash/Shield Parry. Basically,  shield is THE GAMEPLAY.
2. Parrying everywhere. When I got the dodge tutotial during the Dragon flight section- I facepalmed and laughed out loud at the sheer absurdity of it. Like, come on, can we have at least one gameplay section not having the green light dodge/parry mechanics?
3. It took me half the game to adjust and start having fun - first half felt like a slog devoid of challenge and full of tutotials. Gladly, all of this can be skipped on subsequent playthroughs.


Story overall does not matter, it's the game about the vibe and Dark Ages has got it in spades. Everything is metal as hell and the rule of cool matters most.

Overall, solid 7/10.

P.S. Will update the review after the DLC releases

EDIT POST-DLC:

God freaking damn it, with how amazing the DLC is - it's so heartbreaking to see what they did to Id software. Microsoft is evil, there was no reason to kill the hen that produced golden eggs. Feels so empty to look at the trilogy and understand that there won't be a fitting continuation with the big brains behind the systems gone.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game demands hardware capable of ray tracing and requires an NVMe SSD for storage.

citations.review_text:
First off, I want to address the barrier to entry to play this game. This game demands a graphics card capable of ray tracing and an NVME SSD for storage. My computer just barely meets the recommended specifications and it chugs quite a bit even when running at 1080p. I think it was a real shame that players who may have enjoyed the two previous games but were running older hardware were boxed out from trying this game. You might reason that five years had gone by between [i]Doom Eternal[/i] and this game’s launch, giving players ample time to upgrade their hardware. The issue with this rationale, however, is that the current state of the PC component market is utterly abysmal. Anyone that might want to upgrade their hardware right now will have to settle for exorbitant prices (thank you AI) just to afford decent RAM and storage, never mind a powerful enough graphics card. With all of this in mind, the timing of this game’s release and its demanding specifications couldn’t have been worse.

Now, onto the game. This game strays considerably from the formula established in 2016’s [i]Doom[/i] and perfected in [i]Doom Eternal[/i]. While those games had you constantly on the move and making use of platforming and verticality to better position yourself against enemies, this game still has you constantly on the move but it cuts out the platforming and verticality (during combat, at least). If anything, this game actually plays a lot like the original [i]Doom[/i] games did, and I really appreciate that. Some of the levels in this game place you in vast, open arenas and battlefields, a lot like the “city” levels from [i]Doom II[/i]. As a result, enemy encounters also somewhat resemble those from the classic games, spread out over the arena and a bit slower paced compared to those in [i]Doom Eternal[/i]. 

Personally, I find the shield satisfying to use during combat, though I understand some people may feel differently about it, especially with the byproduct of parrying bei…

Fantastic game, better DLC. 100% would recommend to anyone who has played DOOM 2016 at least, if you haven't played that don't play this yet. Wish raytracing wasn't forced but that's like my only real problem.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game includes a setting to remove the slow-motion effect.

citations.review_text:
[h1]The game is much better now than it was on launch.[/h1]

If you didn't like the game when it came out or decided to skip it due to mixed reception, I suggest giving it another try. Since launch id has made many small tweaks to the game such as increasing weapon switch speed, reworking some demon spawns and adding more options like the ability to remove the slowmo.
All of these changes combined have improved the game a lot and made it play way smoother and faster, like a proper Doom game instead of a janky mess that it was on launch.
The forced slowmo was the biggest offender. I hated it, pretty much everyone hated it. And so the very first mod that came out for this game was the slowmo remover. But now you can remove it with a simple toggle in the settings.
Second biggest offender is the inability to bind every weapon to a separate key. That is still the case for some god forsaken reason. Fortunately, Kaibz Mod fixes that which is a must use for Dark Ages imo.

So once you turn off slowmo, install Kaibz Mod and bind all your weapons where you want them to. And then set the parry window to the lowest and enemy projectile speed to the fastest, yeah this becomes a very kickass game. One that can be considered a worthy conclusion to the modern Doom series.

Doom the Dark Ages is above all else: [b]unique[/b]. The shield is not a gimmick, and there hasn't been a single FPS game that integrated parrying and melee combat in it's gameplay design like Dark Ages does. And so while I still have some gripes with it such complete lack of needing to aim. And I think it is in the end, the weakest entry compared to 2016 and Eternal. But it is not by much. And compared to other FPS games released in the past few years, it is still in a league of it's own.
The core principles that made Doom 2016 and Doom Eternal so beloved are still present here. You don't reload, you can only hipfire, your run fast, you punch hard and you leech health and ammo from enemies you kill. An…

Though not quite as big of a hit as eternal, Dark ages was still a blast for any doom fan and created a new and exciting gameplay loop. My two recommendations for eternal fans are removing the slowdown effect and turning on auto run, with the removal of the sprint HUD effect.
